SMTO-SKL-0173 — GitHub couldn't create this pull request

GUID: 30c455b3-19bc-5fd5-97da-fb2a693bc95f
Slug: github-pull-create-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub said no to opening this pull request. Usually the branch with your changes isn't on GitHub yet, the target branch name is wrong, or a pull request for these branches already exists. Nothing was created.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list the open pull requests for your branch, or check the Pull requests tab on github.com. GitHub won't open a second pull request for the same two branches.
  2. Make sure your branch with the changes has been pushed to GitHub. If not, ask the Agent to push it from your project folder first. The GitHub tools in SMTO never push code; the branch must already be on GitHub.
  3. Check that the target branch name (for example main) exists and that your branch has changes it doesn't have, then ask the Agent to create the pull request again. GitHub rejects a pull request into a missing branch or one with no new commits.

What success looks like

  • The new pull request appears in the Pull requests tab on github.com and the Agent shows its number.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, along with both branch names, to the person who manages the GitHub project.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub rejected the pull request creation request with a 422 validation error (for example a missing head or base branch, no commits between them, or an existing open pull request for the same branches).

What this means

  • Pull-request creation receives HTTP 422. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Pull-request creation receives HTTP 422.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact head/base and existing equivalent PRs; the status alone does not identify which constraint failed.

How to fix it

  • Verify that the head branch has been pushed to GitHub (use Git/Shell; the GitHub tools never push), that the base branch exists, that head contains commits not in base, and that no open pull request already exists for the same head and base (github.pull_requests with head="owner:branch"). Then issue a single corrected pull_create.
  • Verify head and base branches exist on GitHub and that no equivalent open PR exists. Use Git/Shell to push the intended branch first; the provider tool never pushes it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported remote branches and a deliberate valid create request are confirmed before another attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
